about: Merum Priorati was founded in 2004 by two Catalan families, with backing from the Pere Ventura family of Cava fame, on the slopes outside Porrera in the eastern Priorat. Only about a quarter of the estate’s 100-plus hectares is planted, across three parcels of terraces cut into mountainsides so steep that the vines are tended entirely by hand and yields can drop to a few hundred grams of fruit per vine. Enologist Roger Oferil makes the wines.

Inici, Catalan for “beginning,” is the estate’s introduction to Priorat. The 2022 blends 60 percent Garnacha with 15 percent each of Cariñena and Syrah and 10 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, all grown on licorella slate. After temperature-controlled fermentation in stainless steel and a gentle pressing, the wine goes into 225-litre French oak barrels for malolactic fermentation and spends eight to twelve months there. Like Destí, it is bottled unfined and unfiltered.

The winery’s notes describe a nose of sun-warmed stone, flowers, balsamic and aniseed, with fresh raspberry and pomegranate on a round, smoky palate. Wine Spectator called the 2022 fresh and graceful, with taut, fine tannins framing dark fruit, licorice and thyme. Wine Enthusiast highlighted crunchy red fruit lifted by fennel, savoury earth, bright acidity and cashmere-soft tannins, while James Suckling noted pepper and racy currant fruit. It is a generous, approachable entry to one of Spain’s most dramatic wine regions.
facts: Steel fermentation; malolactic in French oak; unfined, unfiltered
